title: serving-runtime daily scratchpad 2026-03-29
content:
Date: 2026-03-29
Owner: Ethan Park
Context: personal serving-runtime scratchpad - triage + perf TODOs + kernel notes

TODAY / GOALS
- Triage regression from canary deploy (2026-03-28) where tail-latency spikes for short requests (~<50 tokens) under burst load.
- Follow up on KV-cache invalidation bug reported by QA (INF-3421).
- Try quick kernel change (reduce shared memory contention in attention_v2) and run perf microbench.
- Sync w/ Sofia (SRE) 11:30am - rollout plan for canary rollback vs patch.

PRIOR CONTEXT / RECENT CHANGES
- Canary rolled model routing change that favors batching-friendly path (PR 4123). Observed improved throughput but tail-latency regressions on small requests in production canary.
- QA flagged KV cache invalidation: when model variant toggles, old cache entries not dropped immediately; memory grows until worker restart. Repro steps attached to INF-3421.
- Kernel attention_v2: recent change to reduce register spills (PR 4098) may have introduced a race around shared buffer reuse.

BUG TRIAGE (quick)
- INF-3421 (KV cache invalidation)
  - Symptoms: mem growth over 30 minutes on sustained kicker traffic; eventual OOM in docker container.
  - Suspect: cache eviction race when model variant metadata update interleaves with request serving.
  - Repro: run load with model-switch script (link in ticket). I can repro locally with small dataset in ~15 min.
  - Immediate mitigations: force synchronous cache invalidation during model switch (hotfix flag). Sofia thinks safe for dedicated but prefer patch.
  - Next: write unit test for cache invalidation path + add telemetry metric for "cache-invalidations-per-switch".

- INF-3502 (tail-latency spikes under burst)
  - Symptoms: p95/p99 spikes for <50 token requests when concurrent small requests >200/s.
  - Hypothesis: batching scheduler sometimes builds large batches, causing short requests to wait -> but scheduler has prioritization for short-latency path; maybe prioritization disabled when route policy changed.
  - Quick check: compare scheduler traces between canary and prod (nvprof/NVTX traces). Also check request routing policy toggles in config overlay from 03-28.
  - Action: run synthetic load with short requests and enable logging at scheduler decision points to capture batch sizes & wait times.

PERF EXPERIMENTS / NOTES
- microbench plan (local w/ 2xA100):
  1) Baseline: master commit before PR 4098
  2) Apply revert of PR 4098 (attention_v2 reg change) - measure p50/p95/p99 for 16/128/512 token paths
  3) Apply targeted patch: add atomic fence around shared buffer reuse in attention_v2 (experimental)
- Metrics to capture: tokens/sec, latency histogram, GPU util, SM occupancy, memcpy times, CPU->GPU queue latency.
- NVTX tagging: add tags for scheduler decision boundaries (enqueue, select-batch, dispatch, kv-cache-hit/miss).

KERNEL NOTES / HUNCHES
- attention_v2: observed higher L1 bank conflicts in nvprof when multiple warps hit the same shared offsets - might be due to new packing change.
- Consider moving per-thread offsets to thread-local registers (trade-off with regs usage). If register pressure rises too much, spills/caches cost > benefit.
- Try smaller bank-aware packing (pad stride by 8) to avoid conflicts for typical head-size=64.
- Also check cudaMemPrefetchAsync patterns - maybe we are prefetching too soon and causing stochastic delays.

LOCAL REPRO STEPS
- Start local runtime with env: RUNTIME_PROFILE=nvtx DEBUG_SCHED=1
- Use synthetic generator script: infra/tools/loadgen/small-reqs.sh --rps 250 --concurrency 100 --seq-len 32
- Run for 20 minutes, collect traces at /tmp/nvtx-*.zip

TODO (short)
- [ ] Reproduce INF-3421 locally and write failing unit test (today)
- [ ] Add metric for cache invalidations and hook to console (instrumentation ticket)
- [ ] Run kernel microbench variants and capture nvprof outputs (this afternoon)
- [ ] Draft rollback plan and communicate to platform (Sofia + Priya)
- [ ] Coordinate with product (Jia) on customer impact messaging if rollback needed

MEETING NOTES / ACTIONS
- 11:30 sync w/ Sofia: discuss safe hotfix vs rollback. (Outcome: try hotfix flag for dedicated first; if fails rollback canary.)
- 15:00 team standup: brief on perf experiments + ask for help running larger load tests on staging cluster.

LINKS / TICKETS / PRs
- Jira: INF-3421, INF-3502, INF-3560 (scheduling heuristics)
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123
       https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4098
       https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4145 (wip - atomic fence)
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/serving-runtime-performance
- Slack threads: #serving-runtime (thread ts: 1711234567.012345)

RANDOM NOTES / THOUGHTS
- If we add a short-request fast-path bypass (fully non-blocking, no KV lookup) we could cut p99 dramatically but need correctness checks for tool-calls and func-calling flows.
- Long-term: runway to rewrite scheduler to use per-worker priority queues instead of global assemble queue - expensive but might simplify latency isolation.

END
